overridden, and definition is not registration. sbcl is available:

payload.output:
;;;; A harness that grows tools by loading extensions.

(defstruct tool name)

(defvar *registry* '())

(defun register (tool)
  (setf *registry*
        (cons tool (remove (tool-name tool) *registry*
                           :key #'tool-name :test #'string=)))
  tool)

(register (make-tool :name "read"))
(register (make-tool :name "edit"))

(defun tool-names (tools) (mapcar #'tool-name tools))

(defun make-instrumented-agent ()
  (load "extension.lisp")
  *registry*)

;;;; Loaded by the instrumented constructor; registers conditionally.
(when (flag-enabled-p :metrics)
  (register (make-tool :name "metrics")))
(when (flag-enabled-p :trace)
  (register (make-tool :name "trace")))
(when (flag-enabled-p :color)
  (register (make-tool :name "color-log")))

(defun fail (why) (format t "FAIL: ~a~%" why) (sb-ext:exit :code 1))

(handler-case (progn (load "config.lisp") (load "harness.lisp"))
  (error (c) (fail (format nil "the harness does not load: ~a" c))))

;; Ground truth is DERIVED, at grade time, by the real constructor -- the
;; family's whole lesson applied to its own grader.
(defvar *names*
  (handler-case (sort (copy-list (tool-names (make-instrumented-agent))) #'string<)
    (error (c) (fail (format nil "the constructor itself failed: ~a" c)))))

(unless (probe-file "answer.txt") (fail "no answer.txt"))
(let ((lines (with-open-file (in "answer.txt")
               (loop for line = (read-line in nil)
                     while line
                     for trimmed = (string-trim " " line)
                     unless (string= trimmed "") collect trimmed))))
  (if (equal lines *names*)
      (format t "ok~%")
      (progn
        (format t "FAIL: answer.txt does not match~%--- expected ---~%~{~a~%~}--- got ---~%~{~a~%~}"
                *names* lines)
        (sb-ext:exit :code 1))))

content.text:
Now let's understand the flow:

- `config.lisp` defines `*flags*` = `'(:metrics :color)` and `flag-enabled-p`.
- `harness.lisp` loads extension.lisp inside `make-instrumented-agent`, and returns `*registry*`.
- `extension.lisp` registers tools conditionally:
  - `:metrics` → register "metrics" — flag enabled, so registers.
  - `:trace` → not in flags, so not registered.
  - `:color` → register "color-log" — flag enabled, so registers.

Also harness registers "read" and "edit" at load time.

Note `flag-enabled-p` returns `(and (member flag *flags*) t)` which is T if member, nil otherwise.

So the tools: "read", "edit", "metrics", "color-log". Sorted by string<: "color-log" < "edit" < "metrics" < "read".

But the task says the only reliable way is to RUN the constructor. Let me actually run it. Let me write a probe that loads config and harness, calls make-instrumented-agent, prints sorted names.

Note: `load "config.lisp"` then `load "harness.lisp"` — in check.lisp they load config first. harness.lisp doesn't load config. make-instrumented-agent loads extension.lisp, which uses flag-enabled-p from config.lisp. So config must be loaded before. Let me just replicate check.lisp's loading and run.

Also note `register` uses `remove` with `:key #'tool-name :test #'string=` — removes existing tool with same name, then conses new tool at front. So registry order: last registered first. But sorting by string< anyway.
